newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold ends barely firmer, off early highs.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold ends barely firmer, off early highs.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended marginally higher on Thursday after some of their early gains were pared on the yen's rebound against the dollar late in the day, traders said.
Most-active benchmark February was up two yen at 1,379 yen.
The newly listed May contract finished flat after opening at 1,400 yen. Other prices ranged from one yen to five yen higher.
Gold prices opened higher following gains in New York after Canadian miner Bre-X said its Busang gold deposits in Indonesia may have been overstated, the traders said.
The Bre-X news had little effect on the price of spot gold during Asian hours.
Bullion edged down, quoted at $349.60/350.00 per ounce at 0750 GMT, against $350.10/60 in New York on Wednesday.
In gold futures, private investors were tending to take profits, while trade houses were on the buying side.

Traders said gold futures were confined to recent ranges. "In recent days, private investors were tending to buy gold at around 1,360 yen per gram, while they are quick to sell gold to take profits when gold approaches levels above 1,380 yen," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
Platinum futures ended steady to firmer, while palladium futures were mixed. "With no Russia-related fresh news, the market is basically directionless," one trader said.

Palladium futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to six yen firmer, with benchmark February ending down one yen at 564 yen. Platinum futures ranged from flat to five yen per gram firmer. Benchmark February was up five yen at 1,461 yen.
Benchmark February silver was up 0.3 yen per 10 grams at 204.3 yen.
